lesson.intro: We use the simple present tense for [[habits]] (things we do again and again), [[routines]] and [[facts]] that are always true.
points: I / you / we / they + verb: I [[walk]], they [[play]].
He / she / it + verb + s: she [[walks]], it [[plays]].
Add -es after s, sh, ch, x, o: wash → [[washes]], watch → [[watches]], go → [[goes]].
Consonant + y → change y to i and add -es: cry → [[cries]]. Vowel + y → just add -s: play → plays.
Negative: do not / does not + verb: She [[does not]] like durian.
Questions: Do / Does + subject + verb: [[Does]] he play football?
Signal words: every day, always, usually, often, sometimes, never.

examples.text: My father [[goes]] to work by train.

lesson.tip: After "does" or "does not", the verb has NO -s: Does she play? She does not play.
